error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: timezone is required

solution.content:
1. timezone field is missing from the request body
   - Cause: The JSON body of the POST request completely lacks the timezone field
   - Fix: Add the "timezone" field to the request body using one of the allowed timezone values: "GMT+7", "GMT+8", "GMT-3", for example {"start_date": "2024-01-15", "end_date": "2024-01-31", "timezone": "GMT+8",
 ...}
 2. timezone value is empty or blank
   - Cause: The timezone field value is an empty string "" or contains only whitespace "   ", the @NotBlank validation detects this
   - Fix: Provide a valid timezone value, must be selected from the allowed list: "GMT+7", "GMT+8", "GMT-3", cannot be empty
 3. timezone value is null
   - Cause: timezone is explicitly set to null
   - Fix: Provide a valid timezone value selected from the allowed list: "GMT+7", "GMT+8", "GMT-3"
 4. timezone key name is misspelled
   - Cause: Using a different key name, such as "timeZone" (camelCase) or "time_zone", etc.
   - Fix: Use the correct key name "timezone" (all lowercase, no underscores)

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: granularity is required

solution.content:
1. granularity field is missing from the request body
   - Cause: The JSON body of the POST request completely lacks the granularity field
   - Fix: Add the "granularity" field to the request body using one of the allowed granularity values: "day", "week", "month", "quarter", "year", "customize", for example {"start_date": "2024-01-15", "end_date":
 "2024-01-31", "granularity": "day", ...}
 2. granularity value is empty or blank
   - Cause: The granularity field value is an empty string "" or contains only whitespace "   ", the @NotBlank validation detects this
   - Fix: Provide a valid granularity value, must be selected from the allowed list: "day", "week", "month", "quarter", "year", "customize", cannot be empty
 3. granularity value is null
   - Cause: granularity is explicitly set to null
   - Fix: Provide a valid granularity value selected from the allowed list: "day", "week", "month", "quarter", "year", "customize"
 4. granularity key name is misspelled
   - Cause: Using a different key name, such as "Granularity" or "grain_ularity" or "time_granularity", etc.
   - Fix: Use the correct key name "granularity" (all lowercase, no underscores)
5. granularity value is not in the allowed list
   - Cause: The provided granularity value is not in the allowed granularity list (such as "DAILY", "Daily", "hours", etc.)
   - Fix: Only the following allowed granularity values are supported (case-insensitive, but lowercase is recommended):
       - "day" - daily aggregation
     - "week" - weekly aggregation (starting on Sunday)
     - "month" - monthly aggregation
     - "quarter" - quarterly aggregation
     - "year" - yearly aggregation
     - "customize" - custom date range

error_list.description: currency is invalid

solution.content:

   - Cause: The currency field value in a shop object in shop_list is not an allowed currency type, system throws exception when calling CurrencyEnum.valueOf()

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: session_ids is required

solution.content:
1. an element in session_list is missing the session_ids field
   - Cause: A livestream object in the session_list array does not have the session_ids field
   - Fix: Ensure each object in session_list contains the session_ids field, format: {"shop_id": 123456, "session_ids": [5001, 5002]}
 2. session_ids is an empty array
   - Cause: The session_ids field exists but its value is an empty array []
   - Fix: Provide at least one session_id for each livestream object, session_ids cannot be empty
 3. session_ids value is null
   - Cause: session_ids is explicitly set to null
   - Fix: Provide a valid livestream ID list array, cannot be null

error_list.description: end_date is not ready, please retry later

solution.content:
1. the data corresponding to the requested end_date is still being processed and has not completed
   - Cause: The dashboard data update on the data platform has a delay (usually T-1 or T-2). The data corresponding to the end_date of the current request is still being processed. 
   - Fix: Retry the request later.

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: for day granularity, start_date must equal end_date.

solution.content:
1. start_date and end_date are not the same when using day granularity
   - Cause: When granularity is "day", the system requires querying data for a single date, therefore start_date and end_date must be the same
   - Fix: Set start_date and end_date to the same date. For example, if you want to query daily data for 2024-01-15, set "start_date": "2024-01-15" and "end_date": "2024-01-15"

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: day range is outside the allowed selectable range.

solution.content:
1. selected date is earlier than the earliest allowed date (2 years ago)
   - Cause: The earliest date allowed for querying is 2 years before the current date (calculated according to the timezone). If start_date (for day granularity, start_date must equal end_date) is earlier than
 this date, this error is triggered
   - Fix: The selected date must be within the last 2 years. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, the earliest allowed date for querying is 2024-06-28. Ensure both start_date and end_date are not earlier than
 that date
 2. selected date is later than the latest allowed date (yesterday)
   - Cause: Open API data has a 1-day delay. The latest date allowed for querying is yesterday. If start_date or end_date is today or a future date, this error is triggered
   - Fix: You can only query data up to yesterday. If today is 2026-06-29, you can only query data up to 2026-06-28. Adjust start_date and end_date to yesterday or an earlier date

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: for week granularity, end_date must be within the selected week range

solution.content:
1. end_date is before start_date or outside the selected week range
   - Cause: When granularity is "week", end_date must be within the same week as start_date. The system checks that end_date is less than start_date or end_date exceeds the last day of that week
   - Fix: Ensure end_date >= start_date, and end_date does not exceed the last day of that week. For week granularity, the allowed end_date range is from start_date to 6 days after start_date (or the last day
 before latestSelectableDay, whichever is earlier)
 2. end_date exceeds the last allowed queryable date (yesterday)
   - Cause: The last day of the week in which start_date falls may be a future date, but the system restricts end_date to not exceed yesterday
   - Fix: If the selected week spans yesterday, then end_date should be set to yesterday. For example, if start_date is 2026-06-28 (Sunday), the last day of that week is 2026-07-04 (Saturday), but if today is
 2026-06-29, end_date can be at most 2026-06-28 (yesterday)

solution.content:

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: page_size is only supported when session_list is empty

solution.content:
Explanation:
The page_size parameter enables paginated retrieval of livestream session metrics. It is only valid when querying across all livestream sessions without specifying specific session IDs. When session_list is provided (non-empty), the API returns data for only those specified sessions, making pagination inapplicable.

Possible causes:
- Both session_list (with specific session IDs) and page_size were provided in the same request.

Troubleshooting:
- Remove session_list when using page_size to fetch paginated results across all sessions.
- Alternatively, remove page_size when querying specific sessions by their IDs in session_list.
- For full-scope paginated retrieval: omit session_list, set page_size, and optionally use cursor for subsequent pages.

error_list.description: week start_date is earlier than the earliest allowed week.

solution.content:
1. start_date is earlier than the earliest allowed date (2 years ago)
   - Cause: Open API allows querying data for a maximum of 2 years. The earliest date allowed for querying is 2 years before the current date (calculated according to the timezone). If start_date is earlier than
 this date, this error is triggered
   - Fix: The selected week must be within the last 2 years. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, the earliest allowed Sunday for querying is 2024-06-28. Adjust start_date to a more recent Sunday

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: start_date cannot be later than end_date.

solution.content:
1. start_date is later than end_date
   - Cause: The system checks that start_date is after end_date, which is illogical. For example, start_date is 2026-06-29 and end_date is 2026-06-28
   - Fix: Ensure start_date <= end_date. Adjust the date order so that start_date is earlier than or equal to end_date. For example, the correct way is start_date as "2026-06-28" and end_date as "2026-06-29"

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: month range is outside the allowed selectable range.

solution.content:
1. start_date is earlier than the earliest allowed month (month from 2 years ago)
   - Cause: Open API allows querying data for a maximum of 2 years. The earliest month allowed for querying is the 1st day of that month 2 years ago. If start_date is earlier than this date, this error is
 triggered
   - Fix: The selected month must be within the last 2 years. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, the earliest allowed month for querying is 2024-06-01 (June 2024). Adjust start_date to the 1st day of a more
 recent month
 2. start_date is later than the latest allowed month (current month)
   - Cause: start_date must be the 1st day of a month and cannot exceed the 1st of the current month. If start_date is next month or later, it exceeds the allowed range
   - Fix: Ensure start_date is the 1st of a past or current month. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, start_date can be at most 2026-06-01 (current month)

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: for month granularity, end_date must be within the selected month range.

solution.content:
1. start_date is not the first day of the quarter
   - Cause: When granularity is "quarter", start_date must be the first day of a quarter. The first day of quarters are: Q1 (January 1st), Q2 (April 1st), Q3 (July 1st), Q4 (October 1st). The system checks that
 start_date is not one of these dates
   - Fix: Adjust start_date to the first day of a quarter. For example, if you want to query data for Q2 2026, start_date should be "2026-04-01"; if you want to query Q3, start_date should be "2026-07-01"

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: for quarter granularity, end_date must be within the selected quarter range.

solution.content:
1. end_date is before start_date or outside the selected quarter range
   - Cause: When granularity is "quarter", end_date must be within the same quarter as start_date. The system checks that end_date is less than start_date or end_date exceeds the last day of that quarter
   - Fix: Ensure end_date >= start_date, and end_date does not exceed the last day of that quarter. For quarter granularity, the allowed end_date range is from start_date (first day of quarter) to the last day
 of that quarter (or yesterday, whichever is earlier). For example, Q2 (April 1 to June 30), Q3 (July 1 to September 30), etc.
 2. end_date exceeds the latest allowed queryable date (yesterday)
   - Cause: The last day of the quarter in which start_date falls may be a future date, but the system restricts end_date to not exceed yesterday
   - Fix: If the selected quarter spans yesterday, then end_date should be set to yesterday. For example, if start_date is 2026-07-01 (Q3), the last day of that quarter is 2026-09-30, but if today is 2026-06-29,
 the allowed quarter is Q2 (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-28)

   - Cause: Open API allows querying data for a maximum of 2 years. The earliest year allowed for querying is January 1 of the year 2 years ago. If start_date is earlier than this date, this error is triggered
   - Fix: The selected year must be within the last 2 years. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, the earliest allowed year for querying is 2024 (2024-01-01). Adjust start_date to 2024-01-01 or 2025-01-01 or
 2026-01-01
 2. start_date is later than the latest allowed year (current year)
   - Cause: start_date must be January 1 of a year and cannot exceed January 1 of the current year. If start_date is January 1 of a future year, it exceeds the allowed range
   - Fix: Ensure start_date is January 1 of a past or current year. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, start_date can be at most 2026-01-01 (current year), not 2027-01-01

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: cursor is only supported when session_list is empty.

solution.content:
Explanation:
The cursor parameter enables cursor-based pagination for livestream session metrics. It is only valid for full-scope queries where no specific session IDs are filtered.

Possible causes:
- A cursor value was provided together with a non-empty session_list.

Troubleshooting:
- Omit session_list when using cursor for pagination across all livestream sessions.
- To query specific sessions, remove both page_size and cursor, and provide session IDs in session_list.
- For full-scope paginated retrieval: omit session_list, set page_size, and use the returned cursor in subsequent requests.

solution.content:
1. start_date and end_date span different years
   - Cause: When granularity is "year", end_date must be within the same year as start_date. If start_date is 2025, end_date cannot be 2026 or any other year
   - Fix: Ensure start_date and end_date are in the same year. For example, if you want to query data for 2025, it should be start_date="2025-01-01" and end_date="2025-12-31" (or an earlier date); if you want to
 query 2026, it should be start_date="2026-01-01" and end_date="2026-12-31" (or an earlier date)
2. end_date is later than the latest allowed date (yesterday)
   - Cause: When using year granularity, end_date cannot be later than yesterday. If end_date equals today's date, it exceeds the allowed range for that year
   - Fix: Set end_date to a date not later than yesterday. For example, if today is 2026-06-29, set end_date to 2026-06-28 or earlier to ensure the query is within the allowed range

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: session_list contains duplicate session_id

solution.content:
This error means the request contains duplicate identifiers in the same ID list.

Possible causes:

  • The same session_id appears more than once in the request.
  • Duplicate values are included within a single shop object.
  • The same identifier is repeated unintentionally when constructing the request payload.

How to resolve:

  • Check the corresponding ID list in the request body.
  • Remove duplicate values before sending the request.
  • Ensure each session_id appears only once in the request.

error_list.name: error_param
error_list.description: start_date is required

solution.content:
1. start_date field is missing from the request body
   - Cause: The JSON body of the POST request completely lacks the start_date field
   - Fix: Add "start_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" to the request body, for example {"start_date": "2024-01-15", "end_date": "2024-01-31", ...}
 2. start_date value is empty or blank
   - Cause: The start_date field value is an empty string "" or contains only whitespace "   "
   - Fix: Provide an actual date value in YYYY-MM-DD format, cannot be empty
 3. start_date value is null
   - Cause: start_date is explicitly set to null
   - Fix: Provide a valid date value in YYYY-MM-DD format
 4. start_date key name is misspelled
   - Cause: Using a different key name, such as "startDate" (camelCase) or "start_Date", etc.
   - Fix: Use the correct key name "start_date" (lowercase with underscores)

request_params.description:
Start date of the requested period in YYYY-MM-DD format.

Limitations:

- Must use the YYYY-MM-DD format.

- Must be a valid calendar date.

- Must not be later than end_date.

- Validation is based on the requested timezone.

- The earliest selectable date is calculated as: current day in timezone - 1 day - 2 years.

- The exact boundary rules depend on granularity:

-- For customize, start_date must not be earlier than the earliest selectable date.

-- For day, start_date must equal end_date.

-- For week, start_date must be a Sunday.

-- For month, start_date must be the first day of the month.

-- For quarter, start_date must be the first day of the quarter.

-- For year, start_date must be the first day of the year.
request_params.name: start_date

request_params.description:
End date of the requested period in YYYY-MM-DD format.

Limitations:

- Must use the YYYY-MM-DD format.

- Must be a valid calendar date.

- Must not be earlier than start_date.

- Validation is based on the requested timezone.

- For customize, end_date must not be later than the day before the current day in the requested timezone. The inclusive date range from start_date to end_date must not exceed 366 days.

- For day, end_date must equal start_date.

- For week, end_date must be within the selected week range: from start_date (Sunday) to the end of that Sunday-to-Saturday week, or to the latest selectable day if the week extends beyond today. Formally: startDate ≤ endDate ≤ min(startDate + 6 days, today - 1 day).

- For month, end_date must be within the selected month: from the 1st day of the month to the last calendar day of that month, or to the latest selectable day for the current month. Formally: startDate ≤ endDate ≤ min(month end, today - 1 day).

- For quarter, end_date must be within the selected quarter: from the 1st day of the quarter to the last calendar day of that quarter, or to the latest selectable day for the current quarter. Formally: startDate ≤ endDate ≤ min(quarter end, today - 1 day).

- For year, end_date must be within the selected year: from January 1st to December 31st of that year, or to the latest selectable day for the current year. Formally: startDate ≤ endDate ≤ min(Dec 31, today - 1 day).

request_params.description:
Timezone used for date boundary calculation, selectable date validation, and timestamp conversion.

Limitations:

- Enum values: [\"GMT+7\", \"GMT+8\", \"GMT-3\"]

- The API internally normalizes the open API timezone value for livestream metric queries.

- All date validation rules are evaluated in the requested timezone.
request_params.name: timezone

request_params.description:
Aggregation granularity that determines the validation rules for the requested date range and the reporting period.


Limitations:

- Supported values are customize, day, week, month, quarter, and year.

- customize is validated as a free date range and is internally queried with the affiliate-compatible livestream granularity.

- day represents a single calendar day.

- week requires a Sunday-based calendar week.

- month requires a calendar month range.

- quarter requires a calendar quarter range.

- year requires a calendar year range.

- Any other value is rejected as invalid_parameter.

request_params.description:
List of livestream session query targets.


Limitations:

- Must contain at least one object.

- Must contain at most 100 objects.

- Every shop_id must belong to the specified principal_id.

- Duplicate shop_id values are rejected.

- Each object must provide a non-empty session_ids list.

- Null session_id values are rejected.

- Duplicate session_id values across the whole request are rejected.

- The total number of unique session_ids across the whole request must not exceed 100.

children.description:
Offset to be used in the next request for fetching the next page of detail records.

Notes:

- Returned only when session_list is omitted or an empty array.

- Calculated as cursor + returned_detail_count.

- If returned_detail_count is less than page_size, it indicates there may be no more records.

- If the request is already beyond the end of the result set, the API returns 0 detail records and next_cursor remains equal to the input cursor.

request_sample.value:
<?php

$curl = curl_init();

curl_setopt_array($curl, array(
  CURLOPT_URL => 'https://partner.shopeemobile.com/api/v2/principal/get_session_livestream_performance?access_token=access_token&partner_id=partner_id&principal_id=principal_id&sign=sign&timestamp=timestamp',
  CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
  CURLOPT_ENCODING => '',
  CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS => 10,
  CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 0,
  CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => true,
  CURLOPT_HTTP_VERSION => CURL_HTTP_VERSION_1_1,
  CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => 'POST',
  CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => '{
    "cursor": 0,
    "end_date": "2026-01-31",
    "granularity": "month",
    "page_size": 100,
    "session_list": [
        {
            "currency": "LOCAL",
            "session_ids": [
                1453493,
                1453494
            ],
            "shop_id": 181050132
        }
    ],
    "start_date": "2026-01-01",
    "timezone": "GMT+8"
}',
  CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => array(
    'Content-Type: application/json'
  ),
));

$response = curl_exec($curl);

curl_close($curl);
echo $response;
